plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n * value = 2/3 * value. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $24, so optimal bid ≈ $16, shading down to preserve profit while remaining competitive against Betty and Charles's similarly shaded bids.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bid function for a first-price auction is b(v) = v*(n-1)/n = v*(2/3). My value is $9, so optimal bid ≈ $6. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competing effectively against Andy and Charles.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, where n=3. This gives a bid of value*(2/3). My value is $13, so I'll bid approximately $8.7. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin if I win, following Bayesian-Nash equilibrium logic for symmetric uniform-value first-price auctions.
